article.title: 阅读 Part B · 如何与权力比你大的人表达不同意见
article.context: 文章给出向上级表达反对意见的五步法：判断时机、找共同目标、先征求同意、保持冷静、保持谦逊并把观点表述成可被讨论的意见。
rows: Your boss proposes a new initiative you think won't work.
老板提出一项你认为行不通的新举措。
story
Your senior colleague outlines a project timeline you believe is unrealistic.
资深同事提出一个你认为不现实的项目时间表。
story
What do you say when you disagree with someone who has more power than you do?
当你不同意一个比你更有权力的人时，该怎么说？
ask
How do you decide whether it's worth speaking up?
你如何判断这件事是否值得开口？
ask
And if you do, what exactly should you say?
如果决定说，又究竟该说什么？
ask
Here's how to disagree with someone more powerful than you.
下面就是与权力高于你的人表达不同意见的方法。
advance
You may decide it's best to hold off on voicing your opinion.
你可能会决定暂时不表达意见更好。
qualify
Maybe you haven't finished thinking the problem through, or you want to get a clearer sense of what the group thinks.
也许你还没有把问题想透，或者想先更清楚地了解团队的看法。
explain
If you think other people are going to disagree, too, you might want to gather your army first.
如果你认为其他人也会反对，也许可以先争取支持者。
example
People can contribute experience or information to your thinking—all the things that would make the disagreement stronger or more valid.
别人可以为你的思考补充经验或信息，这些都会让你的反对意见更有力、更站得住脚。
explain
It's also a good idea to delay the conversation if you're in a meeting or other public space.
如果当时在会议或其他公共场合，推迟这场谈话也是好主意。
explain
Discussing the issue in private will make the powerful person feel less threatened.
私下讨论会让权力较大的一方感到没那么受威胁。
conclude
Before you share your thoughts, think about what the powerful person cares about—it may be the credibility of their team or getting a project done on time.
在表达想法前，先想想对方最在意什么——可能是团队的可信度，也可能是项目按时完成。
advance
You're more likely to be heard if you can connect your disagreement to a higher purpose.
如果能把不同意见与更高层次的目标联系起来，你更可能被听进去。
explain
State it overtly, contextualizing your statements so that you're seen not as a disagreeable subordinate but as a colleague who's trying to advance a common objective.
把这个共同目标明确说出来，并为自己的话提供背景，让你看起来不是一个难相处的下属，而是努力推动共同目标的同事。
explain
The discussion will then become more like a chess game than a boxing match.
这样，讨论就更像一盘棋，而不是一场拳击赛。
conclude
This step may sound overly deferential, but it's a smart way to give the powerful person psychological safety and control.
这一步听起来可能过分恭敬，但它能聪明地给对方心理安全感和控制感。
qualify
You can say something like, “I know we seem to be moving toward a first-quarter commitment here—I have reasons to think that won't work, I'd like to lay out my reasoning. Would that be OK?”
你可以这样说：“我知道我们似乎正准备承诺第一季度完成——但我有理由认为这行不通，我想把理由说明一下，可以吗？”
dialogue
This gives the person a choice, allowing him to verbally opt in.
这给了对方选择权，让他可以口头同意继续讨论。
explain
And, assuming he says yes, it will make you feel more confident about voicing your disagreement.
而一旦他答应，你表达不同意见时也会更有信心。
conclude
You might feel your heart racing or your face turning red, but do whatever you can to remain neutral in both your words and actions.
你可能会心跳加速、脸色发红，但要尽一切可能让言语和举止保持中性。
warning
When your body language communicates reluctance or anxiety, it undercuts the message.
当肢体语言传达出犹豫或焦虑时，它会削弱你说出的信息。
explain
It sends a mixed message, and your counterpart gets to choose what signals to read.
这会发出相互矛盾的信号，而对方可以自行选择相信哪一个。
explain
Deep breaths can help, as can speaking more slowly and deliberately.
深呼吸有帮助，放慢语速并更从容地说话也有帮助。
encourage
When we feel panicky, we tend to talk louder and faster.
人在慌张时往往会说得更响、更快。
explain
Simply slowing the pace and talking in an even tone helps the other person cool down and does the same for you.
只要放慢节奏、保持平稳语调，就能帮助对方冷静下来，也能让你自己冷静。
resolve
It also makes you seem confident, even if you aren't.
即使你内心并不自信，这样做也会让你看起来更有把握。
conclude
Emphasize that you're only offering your opinion, not gospel truth.
强调你只是提出自己的观点，而不是宣告绝对真理。
advance
It may be a well-informed, well-researched opinion, but it's still an opinion, so talk tentatively and slightly understate your confidence.
这个观点也许信息充分、研究扎实，但仍只是观点，因此要以试探的口吻表达，并稍微降低自信程度。
qualify
Instead of saying, “If we set an end-of-quarter deadline, we'll never make it,” say, “This is just my opinion, but I don't see how we will make that deadline.”
不要说“如果把截止日期定在季度末，我们绝对完不成”，而可以说“这只是我的看法，但我还看不出我们怎样能赶上这个期限”。
example
Having asserted your position (as a position, not as a fact), demonstrate equal curiosity about other views.
在表明自己的立场——注意，是立场而不是事实——之后，也要对其他观点表现出同等的好奇。
explain
Remind the person that this is your point of view, and then invite critique.
提醒对方这只是你的观点，然后邀请他批评指正。
encourage
Be open to hearing other opinions.
对其他意见保持开放。
conclude
